Phase 2 complete. Gerrit change 1997 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1997),
commit 895a2cd905. NOT closing until it merges.

## Fix

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/access_check.py` (+27/-4, single file). Drops the
module-level `from ...acli import AcliClient` and adds `_default_client(**kwargs)` — a named
factory that imports `AcliClient` INSIDE its body, so the lookup happens at CALL time. Both
frozen defaults (`run_access_check`, `check_mapped_project_visibility`) now point at it.
Production behaviour is byte-identical: same class, same four constructor keywords. An
explicit `client_cls=` never enters the factory, so injection still wins.

This mirrors `_retry_sleep` — the indirection this file already uses for `sleep_fn`, and whose
docstring states the invariant being restored. Deliberately NOT done: weakening the assertion,
adding a retry or sleep, marking the test flaky/xfail, or changing any behaviour.

## RED -> GREEN with a held-out oracle

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_access_check_client_seam.py` (new, 3 tests). It forces the
hostile order itself — imports `access_check` BEFORE patching `acli.AcliClient` — so it is
deterministic in isolation rather than relying on what ran first.

* RED first, for the right reason: `AssertionError: the probe did not use the patched client
  class / assert 0 == 1`. Not an import error, not a typo.
* Held out: the file was moved OUT of the worktree before the fix subagent was dispatched, and
  its path was declared off-limits. The fixer never saw it and self-verified against its own
  scratch reproduction.
* GREEN after: 3 passed.
* Mutation check (teeth): re-seeded the EXACT root cause — restored the module-level import and
  `client_cls=AcliClient` — and the oracle returned to RED (1 failed, 2 passed). Fix restored.
* Refactoring litmus: asserts observable output (returned verdict + step list) and whether the
  injected class was constructed. No private names, no source greps, no intermediate state.

## Replication of the original report

The two-file reproduction that failed 6/6 before now passes 3/3 (20 passed each). The full
sweep is running twice; results follow in a second comment.

## Fix-safety audit

* Restoration, not creation: restores a documented in-file invariant. No new entry point, CLI
  flag, config key, or user-visible artifact.
* No new dependency: the acli import moved from module scope to function scope — same
  dependency, now lazy (which also makes `access_check` more import-safe, since
  `bridge_fsck_visibility` already treats Jira as an optional extra).
* No test weakening: no pre-existing test was touched. Nothing skipped, xfailed, or relaxed.
* Caller-dependency gate: CLEARED. `_lib_ops.py:377` calls with no `client_cls`;
  `jira-capability-probe.py:34` passes one explicitly; `_preflight.py:113` and
  `bridge_fsck_visibility.py:89` inject `probe=`. No caller depends on the default being frozen
  at import, and no test patches `access_check.AcliClient` (all patch the defining module).

## Step 7 sweep

Axis 1 (construct) — an AST pass over all of `src/` for defaults bound to module-level imported
names. 23 raw hits, 9 real injection seams:
* The confirmed one (`access_check.py:99`) — FIXED.
* `access_check.py:396` — the identical construct in the same file, LATENT only because every
  current caller injects `probe=`. FIXED in scope; it is the same seam.
* `_ref_lock.py:558` and `_advisory_lock.py:161` (`sleep_fn=time.sleep`) and
  `metrics/analyzers/_jscpd.py:18` (`run=subprocess.run`) — the same construct, LATENT (all
  current call sites inject explicitly). Filed as `freezing-smooth-godwit`
  (9118-3f70-9a0b-454e), linked `discovered_from` this bug. Out of a bug fix's authorisation:
  refactoring three unrelated modules is not restoring this seam.
* `_commands/_init_probe.py` (`run_git_fn=run_git`) — effectively SAFE; the real consumer passes
  it explicitly and every test patches the consumer. Noted, not filed.

Axis 2 (parity census) — rule: "the access-check probe must resolve its client class at call
time." Five slots:
1. CLI `rebar bridge check-access` -> `_cli/__init__.py:189` spawns a FRESH subprocess running
   `jira-capability-probe.py`, which passes `client_cls=AcliClient` explicitly from its own
   globals. N/A — no in-process import order exists.
2. MCP tool `bridge_check_access` -> `_mcp_reads.py:159` -> `rebar.bridge_check_access()` ->
   the shared core. Covered by the core fix.
3. Library facade `rebar.bridge_check_access()` -> `_lib_ops.py:377` -> the shared core. The
   fixed site.
4. Automated callers (`_preflight.py:113`, `bridge_fsck_visibility.py:89`) inject `probe=`
   explicitly; their `client_cls` default is the :396 site, fixed in scope.
5. Dual-direction: N/A — the probe is one-way.
No MISSING slots: every in-process surface funnels through the one core.

## Residual risk

* The three LATENT frozen-default sites -> ticket filed (`freezing-smooth-godwit`).
* Observed and worth naming: before this fix a `pytest.mark.unit` test was making LIVE Jira
  calls whenever the import order went the wrong way (the runtime probe caught it creating and
  querying real issue keys). That is now impossible through this seam, but there is no
  structural guard preventing a unit-marked test from reaching the network in general.
  ACCEPTED here rather than filed: proposing such a guard is a design decision beyond a bug
  fix, and it has no confirmed second instance.
